nodes.name: Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Next, prepare the reaction solution by adding 0.15 mmol FeCl₂ and 0.15 mmol CoCl₂ to 50 mL of deionized water and stirring thoroughly until completely dissolved. Take 5 mL of the above solution, add 0.03 mmol RuCl₃, and ultrasonically treat for 10 min to obtain the reaction solution. Immerse the cleaned nickel foam (1×3 cm) in the reaction solution for 6 h at room temperature. After the reaction, take out the sample and dry it in vacuum for 8 h to obtain Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.description: HER performance in natural seawater with 1 M KOH (three-electrode)
nodes.source_text: Polarization curves of HER with iR-compensation (compensation ratio of 64%) showed that Ru@FeCo - Ni(OH)_2 exhibited superior catalytic performance of 75mV at 100mAcm^{-2}... Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)_2 maintained stable HER performance for over 3000 h at a high current density of 100 mA cm^{-2}, with an overpotential decay of only 0.015 mV h^{-1} (Figure 4a,f). Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)_2 electrode exhibited a Cdl value of 28.1 mF cm^{-2} for HER

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show clusterlike products of Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets completely covering the nickel foam surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM images of the Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ show that clusterlike products completely cover the NF surface. Upon magnification of these cluster-like products, it can be seen that they are formed by the aggregation of Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets.

properties.description: Low magnification SEM image showing particle aggregate with central void
Higher magnification SEM image showing porous nanoparticle aggregate structure
Highest magnification SEM image with red box highlighting region of interest, showing detailed nanostructure

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM shows ultrasmall Ru crystals (≈5 nm diameter) evenly dispersed in Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets with lattice spacings of 2.15 Å (Ru 002) and 2.65 Å (Ni(OH)₂ 101).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images show that ultrasmall Ru crystals are evenly dispersed in the lamellar Ni(OH)₂ nanosheets, with the Ru crystals having a diameter of ≈5 nm. The red areas exhibit a lattice spacing of 2.15 Å, which attributable to the (002) plane of metallic Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern displays diffraction rings for Ru (002) and Ni(OH)₂ (101) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of the chosen region displays diffraction rings attributable to the (002) plane of Ru and the (101) plane of Ni(OH)₂.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows Ni, Fe, Co, and Ru evenly dispersed; SEM-EDS shows Ru at 7.00 wt.% in Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) elemental mapping of Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ depicts that Ni, Fe, Co, and Ru elements are evenly dispersed on NF surface. The SEM-EDS analysis shows Ru at 7.00 wt.% in Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ catalyst.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP shows Ru content ≈0.4 mg cm⁻² and mass fractions Ru 0.87%, Fe 0.18%, Co 0.16%, Ni 71.59%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma (ICP) analysis indicates that the ruthenium content on the electrode is ≈0.4 mg cm⁻²... the mass fractions of Ru, Fe, Co, and Ni elements are 0.87%, 0.18%, 0.16%, and 71.59%.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS Ni 2p shows Ni²⁺ peaks at 856.03/873.75 eV in Ru@Ni(OH)₂ shifting positively by 0.39 eV (Fe), 0.54 eV (Co), 0.40 eV (FeCo); Ru 3p Ru⁰ peaks shift negatively by 0.66 eV in FeCo; Fe 2p Fe³⁺ at 711.55/723.99 eV; Co 2p Co²⁺ at 781.37/797.27 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Ni 2p high-resolution spectrum of Ru@Ni(OH)₂, two characteristic peaks of Ni²⁺ at ≈856.03 and 873.75 eV... In Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂, the Ni²⁺ peak shows a positive shift of 0.40 eV... Ru⁰ peaks shift to lower binding energies by 0.66 eV... Fe 2p spectrum, two characteristic peaks for Fe³⁺ at 711.55 and 723.99 eV... Co 2p spectrum, two characteristic peaks for Co²⁺ at ≈781.37 and 797.27 eV.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows accelerated reconstruction in Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ with γ-NiOOH peaks at 1.36 V (476, 553 cm⁻¹) vs 1.40 V for undoped.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ru@FeCo-Ni(OH)₂ demonstrated a more rapid structural transformation, with the reconstruction peaks appearing at a lower potential of 1.36 V and achieving full γ-NiOOH formation by 1.38 V.
